name: USGS Offshore Monterey original 2 m seafloor character and bathymetry

producer.name: U.S. Geological Survey and California State University Monterey Bay Seafloor Mapping Lab

rights.license: CC0-1.0; credit USGS and CSU Monterey Bay Seafloor Mapping Lab

spatial.horizontal_crs: EPSG:32610 character grid; EPSG:26910 bathymetry grid
spatial.vertical_datum: NAVD88 for bathymetry; character class has no vertical coordinate

temporal.update_cadence: Static historical grids; monthly catalog and source-integrity check

provenance.access_service: Original USGS Coastal and Marine Geoscience Data System ZIP and FGDC XML downloads
transformations: Verified exact original archive and metadata hashes for both products; opened native GeoTIFFs and counted valid class cells.
Derived 88 generalized, MPA-screened hard-bottom context outlines for research only, with five overlapping historical video observations.
Compared original NAVD88 bathymetry under the historical context outlines without promoting any fishing target.

evidence.supports: Original 1998–2014 video-supervised seafloor classification explains class 3 rock/boulder, the 2 m grid, CC0 terms and research limitations.
Original 1998–2012 bathymetry metadata identifies NAVD88 vertical datum and mixed acoustic/lidar sources.

limitations: The mapped class is historical habitat evidence, not a fish observation or proof of catch success; class and bathymetry share underlying survey evidence.
The source depth grid is NAVD88 and has no per-cell uncertainty companion; it cannot qualify a 200-foot MLLW fishing-depth limit without reviewed conversion and uncertainty.
The cited bounds are the valid character-cell envelope, not continuously surveyed water or a charted reef boundary.

The existing 88 generalized context outlines are not fishing waypoints or chartplotter exports. Current MPAs, federal restrictions, chart hazards, routes and species-specific rules remain independent promotion gates.
Historical video overlap is sparse and not an independent catch record. The products are not for navigation.
